extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students, and practitioners in computational humor and linguistic analysis of jokes
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric for analyzing and constructing 'forced reinterpretation' jokes where a punchline retroactively forces replacement of the obvious reading (R1) with a covert reading (R2). Useful for computational modeling, linguistic analysis, and joke-writing critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage A: Setup admits two interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: The setup text S has at least two valid readings: R1 — the obvious / accessible / preferred reading; and R2 — a non-obvious / hidden but linguistically valid reading. R1 is what virtually all hearers reach by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the surface text genuinely licenses both readings (R1 and R2). The setup must be constructed so the hidden reading is linguistically available even if not salient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage B: Audience commits to R1
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of S, the hearer has fully entered R1's representation of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the setup so that R1 is not merely possible but is the representation the audience adopts before the punchline arrives; this commitment is crucial for the forced switch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage C: Punchline P incompatible with R1 / compatible with R2
rubrics_metrics.description: P is constructed so that P is incompatible with R1 (or jarringly anomalous in R1) and fully compatible with R2 (often natural in R2); the hearer is forced to abandon R1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punchline should create a decisive incompatibility with R1 while fitting cleanly under R2—avoid ambiguous or weak punchlines that do not decisively force reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage D: Reinterpretation under R2
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearer searches for the alternative reading and finds R2. The whole setup retroactively reinterprets under R2, and P now makes sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that after the shift the setup coheres under R2; the retroactive reading should illuminate previously neutral details rather than require ad hoc fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: R1 highly accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: R1 is highly accessible in the setup — the obvious reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make R1 the default for most hearers; if R1 is not salient, the audience may not be surprised or committed and the joke will lose impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: R2 linguistically valid (covert)
rubrics_metrics.description: R2 is linguistically valid in the setup but covert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R2 must be derivable from the setup's wording/structure; it must not be a contrived after-the-fact invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: R1 accessibility high enough to ensure commitment before P
rubrics_metrics.description: R1's accessibility is high enough that the hearer commits to it before P arrives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and pacing of the setup should favor R1 adoption prior to the punchline; if commitment is weak, the forced reinterpretation fails to produce surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: R2 discoverable quickly after P
rubrics_metrics.description: R2 is discoverable quickly enough after P that the joke lands within seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the linguistic cues so listeners can find R2 within the comic time window; too slow discovery yields puzzlement rather than laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: Shift produces the comic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The shift from R1 to R2 produces the comic effect — typically because R2 reveals something incongruous, taboo, or absurd given the setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content revealed by R2 should generate incongruity, surprise, or taboo-related tension appropriate for humor; neutral or trivial shifts won't be funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-property formalization: Compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility — both R1 and R2 are linguistically valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both readings must be defensible interpretations of the setup; if R2 is not truly licensed, the audience will reject the reading and the joke will feel forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-property formalization: Contrast (script opposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast — R1 and R2 differ substantially (script opposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two readings should belong to different scripts or frames so that the switch produces meaningful opposition (e.g., innocent vs. sexual, mundane vs. violent). Strong contrast amplifies the comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-property formalization: Inhibition / conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Inhibition / conflict — P is incompatible with R1, forcing the switch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punchline must create a conflict with R1's assumptions; mere extension of R1 won't force reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model exclusions: non-forced-reinterpretation joke types
rubrics_metrics.description: Forced reinterpretation does NOT cover pure absurdity (no second valid interpretation), pure character-based humor (no setup ambiguity), slapstick (no linguistic R1/R2 structure), or jokes that build comic effect across many beats (no single forced moment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use other theories for these types; do not try to force a reinterpretation analysis onto jokes lacking linguistic ambiguity or a single forcing punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formedness criterion: R1 and R2 genuinely valid (not contrived)
rubrics_metrics.description: A forced reinterpretation joke is 'well-formed' when R1 and R2 are both genuinely valid (not contrived).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making R2 only plausible through strained reinterpretation of words or context; both readings should be plausible without implausible leaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formedness criterion: Accessibility gap is large
rubrics_metrics.description: The accessibility gap is large (R1 obviously preferred over R2 by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft the setup to bias audiences strongly toward R1 so that the switch to R2 is surprising and felicitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formedness criterion: Punchline is sharp
rubrics_metrics.description: P is sharp (it cleanly incompatible with R1, cleanly compatible with R2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer decisive, clear punchlines over vague or equivocal ones; ambiguity in P weakens the forced reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formedness criterion: Strong script opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The script opposition is strong (the two readings are interestingly different).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger script oppositions (e.g., life/death, sexual/innocent) tend to produce more striking comedic effects when the switch occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: R1 not accessible enough
rubrics_metrics.description: If R1 not accessible enough → audience doesn't commit, no surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many hearers entertain R2 concurrently with R1, the punchline will lack the necessary surprise; revise setup to favor R1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: R2 not actually valid
rubrics_metrics.description: If R2 not actually valid → joke feels forced, audience rejects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether naive hearers can plausibly derive R2 from the setup; if not, reword to legitimately license R2 or abandon reinterpretation claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: Punchline ambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: If punchline ambiguous → the switch isn't decisive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity in the punchline can leave audiences unsure which reading to adopt; ensure P distinguishes R2 clearly from R1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: R2 too hard to find
rubrics_metrics.description: If R2 too hard to find → puzzlement instead of comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure cues to R2 are discoverable quickly; overly subtle or obscure R2 will lead to confusion rather than laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic checklist: identifying R1, R2, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic questions: What is R1? What is R2? Are R1 and R2 both genuinely valid in the setup? Is R1 accessible enough that the audience definitely reaches it? Is the punchline incompatible with R1 and compatible with R2? Is R2 discoverable within the comic time window?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions to analyze an existing joke or to test a candidate joke during construction; they summarize the practical tests for forced reinterpretation well-formedness.
